# MikroTik

**Enterprise OID:** 14988.
**Corpus:** one MIB (`MIKROTIK-MIB` — 26 tables, 488 objects) and one
community-generated OpenAPI document (3,652 paths).
**Planes:** RouterOS REST API (the real one), the proprietary binary API on
8728/8729, SSH/CLI, and SNMP. No NETCONF, no RESTCONF, no gNMI, no YANG.

---

## MIKROTIK-MIB

Small but broader than its size suggests — 26 conceptual tables covering
several things bigger vendors need multiple modules for:

| Table | Covers |
|---|---|
| `mtxrInterfaceStatsTable` | per-interface statistics beyond IF-MIB |
| `mtxrOpticalTable` | **transceiver DOM** — one of only eight vendors here with optics over SNMP |
| `mtxrPOETable[interfaceIndex]` | PoE, **ifIndex-keyed** (the easy shape) |
| `mtxrNeighborTable` | MikroTik Neighbor Discovery — MNDP, its own discovery protocol |
| `mtxrQueueSimpleTable[index]`, `mtxrQueueTreeTable[index]` | RouterOS queues — closer to Linux `tc` than to any switch QoS model |
| `mtxrGaugeTable` | generic sensors (voltage, temperature, current, fan) |
| `mtxrPartitionTable` | storage partitions |
| `mtxrScriptTable`, `mtxrScriptRunTable` | **on-device scripts, listed and runnable over SNMP** |
| `mtxrHotspotActiveUsersTable` | hotspot sessions |
| `mtxrWlStatTable`, `mtxrWlRtabTable`, `mtxrWlApTable` | legacy 802.11 (wireless package) |
| `mtxrWlCMTable`, `mtxrWlCMRtabTable`, `mtxrWlCMRemoteTable` | CAPsMAN — MikroTik's controller |
| `mtxrWifiInterfaces`, `mtxrWifiRegistrationTable` | the new `wifi` (802.11ax) stack |
| `mtxrWl60GTable`, `mtxrWl60GStaTable` | 60 GHz (wAP 60G) |
| `mtxrLTEModemTable`, `mtxrLTECarrierAggTable` | cellular |
| `mtxrIkeSATable` | IPsec security associations |
| `mtxrRemoteCapTable` | remote packet capture |
| `mtxrDnStatTable` | dynamic DNS |

Plus the `mtxrSystem` scalars (uptime, CPU, memory, board name, firmware,
serial), and HOST-RESOURCES / UCD-SNMP underneath because RouterOS is Linux.

**Two wireless stacks in one MIB.** `mtxrWl*` is the legacy `/interface
wireless` package and `mtxrWifi*` is the new `/interface wifi` (wifiwave2)
stack. A device runs one or the other depending on RouterOS version and
hardware; both sets of tables exist in the MIB and only one is populated.

---

## The RouterOS REST API

`spec/openapi/mikrotik/routeros-7.24-openapi.json` — OpenAPI 3.0.3, **3,652
paths**, the largest single API surface in the corpus by path count.

Path distribution:

```
878  /interface/...     every interface type and its sub-menus
858  /ip/...            addressing, routes, firewall, DHCP, DNS, services
572  /routing/...       BGP, OSPF, filters, tables
314  /system/...        resource, identity, clock, scheduler, scripts, package
248  /ipv6/...
236  /tool/...          ping, traceroute, bandwidth-test, netwatch, sniffer
154  /mpls/...
 67  /certificate/...
 46  /user/...   42 /queue/...   40 /ppp/...   25 /disk/...
 20  /radius/... 17 /port/...    16 /snmp/...
```

### What it is and is not

**It is not official.** MikroTik publishes no machine-readable spec for the REST
API (there is an open feature request). This document is generated by the
community `restraml` project, which runs `/console/inspect` against a live
RouterOS instance and emits OpenAPI from the console command tree.

**Consequences**, already recorded in `spec/openapi/mikrotik/SOURCES.md`:

- Endpoints and argument *names* are accurate — they come from the console
  itself.
- Argument *types* are frequently `any`.
- Response schemas are imprecise.
- There are no descriptions.

So it is a reliable map of *what you can call* and an unreliable one of *what
comes back*. Treat responses as untyped JSON and validate at the decoder.

### The REST API mirrors the console

Every path corresponds to a console menu: `/ip/address`, `/interface/bridge/port`,
`/ip/firewall/filter`, `/routing/bgp/connection`. Verbs are `GET` (print),
`PUT` (add), `PATCH` (set), `DELETE` (remove), plus `POST` for command
endpoints. The `.id` field is RouterOS's internal row identifier (`*1`, `*2`, …)
and is **not stable across reboots**.

---

## SwOS

The CSS/CRS switch-only firmware. SNMP read-only, no REST API. `MIKROTIK-MIB`
covers it, thinly. Recorded in `spec/openapi/mikrotik/SOURCES.md`.

---

## Practical guidance

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Interface inventory and state | REST `/interface`, or IF-MIB |
| Optics | `mtxrOpticalTable`, or REST `/interface/ethernet/monitor` |
| PoE | `mtxrPOETable` — ifIndex-keyed, unusually easy |
| Neighbours | `mtxrNeighborTable` (MNDP); LLDP if enabled |
| Bridge / VLAN | **REST only** — MikroTik's bridge VLAN model has no MIB representation |
| Routing | REST `/ip/route`, `/routing/*` |
| Firewall / NAT | REST only |
| Wireless | `mtxrWifi*` or `mtxrWl*` depending on stack; CAPsMAN via `mtxrWlCM*` |
| Config backup | REST `/system/backup`, `/export` |

**The gap that matters:** MikroTik's bridge and VLAN configuration — the thing
that determines L2 behaviour on a CRS switch — is not in the MIB at all. Any
FlowSeer L2 model for MikroTik has to go through REST.

---

## Traps

- `.id` values are not stable identifiers; use the named field (`name`,
  `interface`, `address`) where one exists.
- RouterOS distinguishes `/interface/ethernet` (the physical port) from
  `/interface/bridge/port` (its bridge membership) from `/interface/vlan` (a
  tagged sub-interface). Three menus, one conceptual interface tree.
- The two wireless stacks are mutually exclusive per device.
- SNMP must be explicitly enabled and is off by default; the REST service
  (`www-ssl`) likewise.
